title: compat.go bridges flat AMConfigV1.Receivers to nested DB/API Receivers shape
answers: Why does AMConfigDB still nest receivers under AlertmanagerConfig while the in-memory model has them top-level?
Where do I update receiver (de)serialization when adding a new receiver-related field?
How are receivers round-tripped between the Go model and the stored/API JSON config?
body:
Symptom: receivers disappear or duplicate after a DB save/load round-trip, or a new receiver field doesn't show up in the stored AMConfigDB/API JSON.
Root cause: the DB/API JSON shape (definition.PostableApiAlertingConfig, used inside AMConfigDB) still nests Receivers under AlertmanagerConfig, while the in-memory v1.AMConfigV1.Receivers is a top-level field — these two shapes are intentionally asymmetric and bridged manually.
Fix pattern: ToModel maps in.AlertmanagerConfig.Receivers into the top-level AMConfigV1.Receivers via ReceiversToModel; ToDBModel/PostableApiAlertingConfigToDB map AMConfigV1.Receivers back into the nested definition.PostableApiAlertingConfig.Receivers via ReceiversToDB. Any change to how receivers are represented must update both directions together.
Constraints: applies only to the v1 compat layer that converts between AMConfigV1 and the stored/API AlertmanagerConfig representation; does not apply if you're only touching the in-memory model.

search: compat.go in pkg/services/ngalert/notifier/legacy_storage/v1/ bridges the intentionally asymmetric shapes between flat in-memory AMConfigV1.Receivers (top-level field) and nested DB/API definition.PostableApiAlertingConfig.Receivers (nested under AlertmanagerConfig). ToModel uses ReceiversToModel to flatten, and ToDBModel/PostableApiAlertingConfigToDB use ReceiversToDB to nest; any receiver field change must update both directions together. This applies only to the v1 compat layer for converting between in-memory and stored/API representations; it does not apply if modifying only the in-memory model.
